title: Wheat export prices climb as Black Sea shipments slow
summary: Export prices for milling wheat rose to USD 248 a tonne as port congestion and higher freight rates slowed Black Sea shipments.

articles.title: Wheat export prices climb as Black Sea shipments slow
articles.text:
Export prices for milling wheat from Black Sea ports rose to USD 248 a tonne this week, up 6% from a month earlier, traders said.

Shipments slowed because of port congestion and a 15% jump in freight rates for Handysize vessels. Buyers in Turkey and Egypt, the largest importers in the region, delayed new purchases while waiting for prices to settle.

Analysts expect prices to stay firm until the end of the year, but warn that a stronger local currency could cut exporters' earnings when converted.
